topic: Function Overloading and Type Equivalence in C++
explanation: In C++, function overloading allows multiple functions to have the same name but different parameter types or counts. However, when parameter types are declared using typedefs (type aliases), they are considered equivalent to the underlying types, and functions with parameters declared using equivalent typedefs are not considered overloads but redeclarations of the same function. This concept emphasizes that typedefs do not create new types but serve as synonyms, affecting function overloading resolution and linkage.
keywords: typedef function overloading, typedef type equivalence, typedef overloading resolution
